questions.question: Ramlal marks up his goods by 40% and gives a discount of 10%. What is his net profit percentage?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For successive percentage changes, use the net effect formula: Net % = a + b + (a × b) ÷ 100

Here, Markup (a) = +40% and Discount (b) = −10%

Net Profit % = 40 − 10 + [40 × (−10)] ÷ 100

Net Profit % = 30 − 4 = 26%

**∴ The correct answer is 26%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Markup Percentage = 40%

Discount Percentage = 10%

**Formula Used:**

SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100

Profit % = [(SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/648b541e29f9eb1e8917f94774372ff3c9a49a15fd6e46c915a4c6afa9608b03.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the Cost Price (CP) of the goods be 100.

⇒ Marked Price (MP) = 100 + (40% of 100) = 140

⇒ Discount given = 10% on MP = (10 ÷ 100) × 140 = 14

⇒ Selling Price (SP) = MP − Discount

⇒ SP = 140 − 14 = 126

⇒ Profit = SP − CP = 126 − 100 = 26

⇒ Net Profit Percentage = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

⇒ Net Profit Percentage = (26 ÷ 100) × 100 = 26%

**∴ The correct answer is 26%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price vs Cost Price

Marked Price (MP) is always calculated by applying the markup percentage on the Cost Price (CP). Formula: MP = CP × (100 + Markup%) ÷ 100.

Successive Percentage Change

When a value undergoes two successive percentage changes of a% and b%, the net effective change is given by the formula: a + b + (a × b) ÷ 100.

Discount Calculation

Discount is always applied on the Marked Price (MP), never on the Cost Price. Formula: SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100.

Direct CP to MP Ratio

The direct relationship between Cost Price and Marked Price is given by the ratio: CP ÷ MP = (100 − Discount%) ÷ (100 + Profit%).

questions.question: A shop provides flat 50% discount on one shirt, while another shop provides two successive discounts of 30% and 30%. If the difference in the bill is ₹43, then find the cost of the shirt.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective discount of successive 30% and 30% = 30 + 30 − (30 × 30) / 100 = 51%.

Difference in effective discounts = 51% − 50% = 1%.

The difference in the bill amount is directly equal to the 1% difference in discount.

1% of Cost = ₹43 ⇒ 100% of Cost = ₹43 × 100 = ₹4,300.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹4,300.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First shop offers a flat discount = 50%

Second shop offers successive discounts = 30% and 30%

Difference in the final bill amount = ₹43

**Formula Used:**

Effective discount for two successive discounts a% and b% = (a + b − ab / 100)%

 
 Cost = 100%

 

 Flat 50% Off
 
 
 Bill 1 = 50%

 

 30% and 30% Off
 
 
 Bill 2 = 49%

 

 Diff = 1%
 
 
 1% = ₹43 → 100% = ₹4300

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the cost (marked price) of the shirt be ₹x.

⇒ Bill amount from the first shop (after 50% off) = x − 0.50x = 0.50x

⇒ Effective discount by the second shop = 30 + 30 − (30 × 30) / 100 = 60 − 9 = 51%

⇒ Bill amount from the second shop = x − 0.51x = 0.49x

⇒ Difference in the bills = 0.50x − 0.49x = 0.01x

⇒ We are given that the difference is ₹43.

⇒ 0.01x = 43

⇒ x = 43 / 0.01 = 4300

**∴ The correct answer is ₹4,300.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discount Formula

When two discounts of a% and b% are given successively, the equivalent single discount is derived directly using the formula (a + b − ab/100)%.

Marked Price and Selling Price

Selling Price (Bill Amount) = Marked Price − Discount. The absolute difference between the two bill amounts equates strictly to the difference in the applied discount percentages calculated on the Marked Price.

Three Successive Discounts

For three successive discounts a%, b% and c%, apply the formula first to find the equivalent of a% and b%, say d%. Then apply the formula again for d% and c% to find the final effective percentage.

questions.question: A shopkeeper bought 20 chairs for ​₹18,000. On selling them he had a gain equal to the selling price of four chairs. What is the selling price of each chair?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A shopkeeper bought 20 chairs for ​₹18,000

On selling them he had a gain equal to the selling price of four chairs

**Calculation:**

Profit = (S.P. of 20 chairs) − (C.P. of 20 chairs)

⇒ S.P. of 4 chairs = S.P. of 20 chairs − C.P. of 20 chairs

⇒ S.P. of 16 chairs = C.P. of 20 chairs

⇒ S.P. of 16 chairs = 18000

⇒ S.P. of 1 chair = Rs. 18000/16

⇒ Rs 1125

**∴ The selling price of each chair is Rs. 1125.**

questions.question: College P has 180 students scoring average marks of 88 and college Q has 320 students scoring average marks of 72. Find the average marks of both the colleges together.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of students in College P and Q = 180 : 320 = 9 : 16.

Assume base average = 72.

Deviation of P from base = 88 − 72 = 16.

Weighted deviation = (9 × 16) ÷ (9 + 16) = 144 ÷ 25 = 5.76.

Total Average = 72 + 5.76 = 77.76.

**∴ The correct answer is 77.76.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of students in P (n₁) = 180, Average of P (A₁) = 88.

Number of students in Q (n₂) = 320, Average of Q (A₂) = 72.

**Formula Used:**

Combined Average = (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂)

 College P
 
 Avg: 88
 (180 Students)
 College Q
 
 Avg: 72
 (320 Students)
 
• 
 
 Combined Average = 77.76

⇒ Total marks for P = 180 × 88 = 15840

⇒ Total marks for Q = 320 × 72 = 23040

⇒ Combined marks = 15840 + 23040 = 38880

⇒ Total students = 180 + 320 = 500

⇒ Combined Average = 38880 ÷ 500 = 77.76

**∴ The correct answer is 77.76.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average Concept

Weighted Average = Σ(Valueᵢ × Weightᵢ) ÷ ΣWeightᵢ. In this context, students are the weights.

Range of Average

The combined average of two groups always lies between the minimum average and the maximum average (72 < 77.76 < 88).

Alligation Method

The ratio of students can be found if the averages are known: (AvgP − AvgMᵢₓ) ÷ (AvgMᵢₓ − AvgQ) = nQ ÷ nP.</p

questions.question: A car travels the first 160 km at a speed of 64 km/h and the next 160 km at a speed of 80 km/hr What is the average speed for the first 320 km of the tour?

Speed for the first 160 km = 64 km/h

Speed for the second 160 km = 80 km/h 

**Formula used:**

Average speed = total distance/total time taken

Time taken to cover a certain distance = distance/speed

**Calculation:**

Total distance = 160 + 160 = 320 km

Time taken to cover the 160 km distance at 64 km/h = 160/64

⇒ 10/4 hours = 2.5 hours

Time taken to cover the 160 km distance at 80 km/h = 160/80

⇒ 2 hours

Total time taken to cover the distance of 320 km = 2 + 2.5 = 4.5 hours

Average speed = 320/4.5

⇒ 640/9 = 71.11 km/h
